newsitem.title: INDIA: India to promote hydropower, coal shipment.
newsitem.headline: India to promote hydropower, coal shipment.

text.p: India will encourage the exploitation of hydropower potential and the transport of coal by ships to coastal power plants to help plug a power shortfall, Power Minister Y.K. Alagh said on Wednesday.
"We want to reduce peaking shortage, and these measures would improve the supply of electricity in the short run," Alagh told a workshop on privatising transmission and distribution of power.

He said that demand management was critical. The government is in the process of setting up a an Energy Conservation Authority, to supplement its current initiatives in building general awareness about end-use efficiency, the minister said.

Alagh said that during the ninth five year plan covering 1997 to 2002, 560 billion rupees ($15.6 billion) will be required for transmission and distribution. He expected the private sector to invest 200 billion rupees in this sector during the period.
He said the ratio of investment in generation, transmission, distribution and rural electrification should be four-to-two-to-one-to-one.

A legal, administrative and financial framework will be adopted for the power transmission sector, the minister said. A committee has been set up for this, and is expected to give its report soon, he said.

"In addition to reviewing existing arrangements for planning and approval of transmission projects, the committee has been asked to formulate guidelines for determination of transmission tariff and framework for negotiating transmission service agreements," Alagh said.
He added that the committee will also look at selection of private companies, regulation of transmission projects through licences and coordination of regional grid operations. ($1 = 35.8 rupees)
